article.headline: Letting a video model revise its next action
article.lead: WorldGuide selects actions from the visual state it has already generated, closing the loop during a procedural task. SpaceFlow gives an artist local control over 3D geometry through text and primitives. Each offers a way to correct a generation before accepting the result.

picks.question: Which failed tasks come from choosing the wrong next action, and which come from rendering a chosen action incorrectly?

paragraphs.text: WorldGuide feeds generated visual states back into its planner to choose the next step of a procedure. SpaceFlow gives a human a more local kind of control: text and geometric primitives constrain different parts of a 3D generation without training a new model. In both cases, success depends on whether a requested change reaches the intended part of the output.

Pumpire tests whether a 3D foundation model can estimate the metric distance between two points using images or video. FreeMatching addresses the complementary problem of identifying corresponding points across views, with applications to reference-guided generation and editing. A match identifies which points to compare; a distance estimate puts a scale on them.

sections.heading: Training across tasks and fitting inference into memory

paragraphs.text: Hebero offers a GPU-parallel setting for training and evaluating reinforcement learning across 40 heterogeneous tasks. AirLLM targets inference on constrained hardware: its repository describes running a 70B language model with a single 4GB GPU. For the latter, fitting the weights and achieving useful token throughput are separate questions.
